channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: Stefon Diggs caught 5-of-9 targets for 35 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
item.description:
Stefon Diggs WAS Wide Receiver

Diggs was the Commanders’ No. 1 receiver with Terry McLaurin out. That was good for a 24 percent target share and a handful of PPR points, but not much else. Marcus Mariota went down on the second drive and Athan Kaliakmanis took his place for the remainder of the game. Kaliakmanis made a few big throws but the offense struggled on the whole. Diggs could be in line for a big boost in fantasy production if Jayden Daniels is back next week, but McLaurin could just as easily return and take back his WR1 role. Diggs’ Week 5 fantasy outlook could swing wildly depending on how those injuries shake out this week.

item.title: FOX Sports’ Erin Andrews reports that Puka Nacua has been dealing with a “pre-hernia” injury.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Andrews broke the news while reporting from the sideline of the Rams’ Week 4 game against the Eagles. Signs have been pointing to this type of injury for a while now, with the Rams referring to Nacua’s nagging injury as both a hip and groin issue. Just over two minutes remain in the third quarter, and Nacua has only come off the field for a few plays thus far. It appears as though the team has handled the injury well, though one imagines re-injury risk is still a factor. That said, he is a WR1 whenever he is active.

item.title: Treylon Burks caught 1-of-3 targets for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks only catch of the day came on a double-move that saw him burn Sauce Gardner for a massive touchdown, though he may have simply been working back to the quarterback before realizing the throw was going over his head. Either way, Burks turned on the jets, tracked down the ball, and ran in the Commanders’ only touchdown of the day. Burks isn’t on the fantasy radar despite the long catch, but it’s nice to see him carving out a role in Washington.

item.title: Broncos declared OLB Dondrea Tillman, QB Sam Ehlinger, TE Dallen Bentley, DL Tyler Onyedim, and OL Kage Casey inactive for Week 4 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Dondrea Tillman DEN Outside Linebacker

The Broncos head into Week 4 as one of the healthiest teams in the league. They will be without Tillman and Onyedim, however. Denver’s defense will look to slow down the red-hot Niners offense.

item.title: Chig Okonkwo caught 2-of-4 targets for five yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo was back in action today after missing the last two games with a hamstring issue. With Marcus Mariota exiting this game early because of an injury, the passing attack was out of whack from the jump. There wasn’t much of a chance to reinstall Okonkwo into the mix this week. The hope is that he will earn more work with Jayden Daniels potentially back in the lineup in Week 5, but fantasy managers will need to see it to believe it with Okonkwo.

item.title: Mike Evans (ribs) is active for Week 4 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans will battle through his rib injury and suit up against Denver, though it remains to be seen whether the veteran will play a full complement of snaps. Through three games Evans has accounted for 22 percent of he 49ers’ targets and 30 percent of the team’s air yards. The Niners declared QB Kurtis Rourke, DE Nick Bosa, DT James Thompson Jr., RB Jordan James, LB Tatum Bethune, CB Ephesians Prysock, and OT Enrique Cruz Jr. inactive against the Broncos.

item.title: Dee Alford is questionable to return to Week 4 against the Patriots with an ankle injury.
item.description:
Dee Alford BUF Cornerback

Alford was injured in a pile while making a tackle in the third quarter. His backup, Te’Cory Couch, has already been injured in this game as well. That means that the Bills will turn to practice squad call-up Kani Walker or safety Damar Hamlin as their slot corner.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Ravens RG Andrew Vorhees (foot) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 4’s game against the Titans.
item.description:
Andrew Vorhees BAL OFFENSIVE GUARD (SUB)

Vorhees exited late in the first half against the Titans and was replaced by Emery Jones. Vorhees was making his first start of the season this week and played on just eight snaps in last week’s game against the Cowboys. Hopefully this isn’t anything too serious, as the Ravens’ interior offensive line has already been hit with multiple injuries this season.

item.title: Edgerrin Cooper suffered an Achilles injury in Week 4 against the Bucs and will not return.
item.description:
Edgerrin Cooper GB Linebacker

Cooper went down with a non-contact injury and had to be carted from the field. The team ruled him out shortly after he left the field. Unfortunately, this looks like a torn Achilles for the young linebacker.

item.title: Dyami Brown caught 3-of-4 targets for 65 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
item.description:
Dyami Brown WAS Wide Receiver

Third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis took over early in this game and the two backups quickly formed a connection. Kaliakmanis hit him on a 48-yard strike in the third quarter for the team’s longest offensive play of the day. Kaliakmanis couldn’t get much else going, but the long catch alone was enough to lead the Commanders in receiving yards. By targets, Brown was still the team’s WR3, so fantasy managers shouldn’t worry about adding him off the waiver wire ahead of Week 5.

item.title: Ed Oliver is questionable to return with a knee injury.
item.description:
Ed Oliver BUF Defensive Lineman

It’s unclear when Oliver got hurt or what happened. He was on the bench without a helmet for a few drives before heading into the locker room. The Bills are down 21-17, and without T.J. Sanders as well, so they can’t afford to lose Oliver.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Chiefs declared TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier, DB Jadon Canady, DE Jack Pyburn, OT Diego Pounds, and OT Josh Simmons inactive for Week 4 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Garrett Nussmeier KC Quarterback

There’s nothing surprising here. The only injury is to Simmons, who was ruled out before the weekend and will once again be replaced by Kahlil Benson, who has yet to allow a sack in three games this season.

Source: Matt McMullen

item.title: Mack Hollins is questionable to return with a calf injury
item.description:
Mack Hollins NE Wide Receiver

Hollins went down when he cut to the sideline on an out route. He had to hobble off the field and was immediately taken into the locker room. The Patriots have not ruled him out yet, but we’d be surprised if he returned today. Romeo Doubs should continue to see the vast majority of targets.

Source: Mark Daniels

item.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee/illness) will play in Week 4 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Despite being questionable with a knee injury and an illness that was announced early Sunday, Bowers is active in what’s a surprisingly pivotal Week 4 matchup between undefeated AFC West teams. Bowers caught 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown on 14 targets last week and will be a high-end TE1 this week. While Bowers is active, the Raiders did declare QB Aidan O’Connell, CB Darrell Luter Jr., S Tristin McCollum, OL Jackson Powers-Johnson, and DT Jonah Laulu inactive for Week 4.

Source: Las Vegas Raiders

item.title: Austin Ekeler rushed four times for 29 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, adding one catch for 11 yards.
item.description:
Austin Ekeler WAS Running Back

Ekeler made his 2026 debut in London and immediately operated as the Commanders’ backup with Rachaad White out. The team did, however, give four running backs multiple touches in this game. Ekeler’s role could grow as he gets more reps under his belt this year, but he could just as easily be made inactive once White is healthy. He’s only worth stashing in the deepest of leagues.

item.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 4 against the Titans.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Lamar was sacked on the Ravens’ final play of the first half. His ankle got caught under Titans EDGE Jermaine Johnson on the play, and when the Ravens took the field in the third quarter, it was backup Tyler Huntley who was under center. With the Ravens holding a 24-7 lead, it wouldn’t be surprising if the Ravens opted to play it safe with Jackson and keep him out for the remainder of this one.

item.title: Bengals WR Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will not return Week 4 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

Chase exited in the first half after his facemask was pulled by a Jaguars defender and his head slammed against the ground. He headed to the locker room to be evaluated for the concussion and was promptly ruled out coming out of halftime. Chase’s day ends after catching three targets for 27 yards. Tee Higgins will see a big boost in targets with Chase out while Dohnte Meyers will also see an uptick in usage.

item.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed nine times for 15 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, adding two catches for 35 yards.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

Bill was surprisingly involved through the air, seeing four targets, one of which he took down the sideline for a 35-yard gain early in the match. On the other hand, three different Commanders backup running backs touched the ball today. Austin Ekeler led the way with four carries. Kaytron Allen and Craig Reynolds combined for another five attempts. The Commanders have had commitment issues with Croskey-Merritt dating back to his rookie season and nothing has changed this year. He will be stuck in the back of the RB3 ranks for Week 5 against the Giants.

item.title: Vikings declared WR Justin Jefferson, S Jakobe Thomas, QB Max Brosmer, P Brett Thorson, CB Chuck Demmings and DL Elijah Williams inactive for Week 4 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

Jefferson injured his ankle in Week 3 and reportedly “got close” to returning to the game. Holding him out appears to have been the right call. He did not practice at all this week. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported yesterday that Jefferson is “hopeful” to play in Week 5 against the Saints. Jefferson’s Week 4 absence elevates Jordan Addison to the top receiving role.

Source: Minnesota Vikings

item.title: Te’Cory Couch (hamstring) is doubtful to return to Week 4 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Te'Cory Couch BUF Defensive Back

Couch is on the field for the Bills as a depth player with Christian Benford (toe) sidelined. It seems that the Bills will now be down yet another cornerback for the remainder of this game.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Dolphins declared WR Caleb Douglas, QB Brady Cook, CB Marcellas Dial, EDGE Rob Beal, OG DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 4 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

The Vikings will be without Douglas, one of their two talented rookie wide receivers, against the Vikings’ top-tier defense today. He is sidelined by an ankle injury. Joly, the Dolphins’ rookie tight end, is inactive after making his debut last week. Cook wil serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

Source: Miami Dolphins

item.title: Athan Kaliakmanis completed 15-of-33 passes for 186 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Commanders’ 30-13, Week 4 loss to the Colts.
item.description:
Athan Kaliakmanis WAS Quarterback

Marcus Mariota suffered a knee injury at the end of the Commanders’ second drive. He was later ruled out for the rest of the game, resulting in Kaliakmanis’ first NFL action. He tried to chuck it deep like Mariota has done so far, but the results weren’t nearly as pretty. He averaged 5.3 yards per attempt and completed 45.5 percent of his passes. Kaliakmanis did find Treylon Burks for a 47-yard bomb in the third quarter, so it wasn’t all bad. Mariota is likely out next week, but Jayden Daniels has a good shot at returning. Assuming he does, Kaliakmanis will return to backup duties versus the Giants.

item.title: Seth McGowan rushed six times for 31 yards in the Colts’ Week 4 win over the Commanders, adding one catch for seven yards.
item.description:
Seth McGowan IND Running Back

McGowan got a whole drive to himself early in the second quarter. Three of his carries and one of his two targets came on this drive. He was otherwise tasked with normal backup duties. McGowan is the only backup of note on the team, but he doesn’t have a standalone fantasy role right now.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) will not return to the Eagles’ Week 4 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley was injured on the Eagles’ second series and officially ruled out midway through the second quarter. He had only two carries for eight yards before departing. It has been mostly Tank Bigsby since, though Will Shipley has received a smattering of handles. Already banged up this season, Barkley is probably in real danger of missing Week 5 against the Jaguars in London.

item.title: DJ Moore is doubtful to return to Week 4 against the Patriots.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Moore landed on his left shoulder while trying to make the catch on a pass in the second quarter. It’s the same shoulder that he injured in the Week 2 win over the Lions. Obviously, the fact that it’s the same shoulder is not a great sign, as is Moore’s long injury history. We should get an update at halftime, but Keon Coleman figures to step into a larger role for the remainder of the game.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Tyler Warren caught all five of his targets for 41 yards in the Colts’ Week 4 win over the Commanders.
item.description:
Tyler Warren IND Tight End

Warren tied for a team high in catches but was out-targeted by Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin. If you couldn’t tell, the passing attack did not look good. Daniel Jones was horribly inaccurate and the Commanders were largely successful in slowing down Warren and Josh Downs. Better days should be ahead for Warren, but he’s averaging a dismal 32.5 yards per game right now. He’s falling to the back of the TE1 ranks ahead of Indy’s Week 5 date with Pittsburgh.

item.title: Ashton Dulin caught 3-of-6 targets for 29 yards in the Colts’ Week 4
item.description:
Ashton Dulin IND Wide Receiver

Dulin was active for the first time this year. His return could not have come at a better time with Keenan Allen ruled out over the weekend. Dulin took on a starting role and wound up leading the team in targets, tied with Laquon Treadwell. The Colts couldn’t get much going through the air and settled for spreading the ball around instead of peppering their top pass-catchers with targets. It’s hard to imagine them taking that approach again in Week 5. Even if they do, Dulin is more of a thorn in the sides of Tyler Warren and Josh Downs than a FLEX option in his own right.

item.title: Bengals WR Ja’Marr Chase (concussion evaluation) is questionable to return Week 4 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

Chase was injured after a second quarter facemask penalty by a Jaguars defender. His neck whipped back as he was taken to the ground and he promptly exited the game. After a brief amount of time in the blue tent, Chase headed to the locker room. The Bengals announced he is being evaluated for a concussion but a locker room visit indicates Chase is on the wrong side of questionable.

Source: Cincinnati Bengals

item.title: Saquon Barkley was forced from the Eagles’ Week 4 game against the Rams with a hamstring injury and is questionable to return.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley pulled up on a strong run on the Eagles’ second series. He dropped the ball out of bounds and appeared to be in a heap of pain, hopping around on one leg before taking a knee. He spent some time in the tent before making his way slowly to the locker room. Barkley pulls up not infrequently, but this had the looks of an issue likely to end his afternoon. Tank Bigsby was the next man up, taking a huge third down loss. Will Shipley should mix in, as well, if Barkley’s afternoon is indeed through.

item.title: Jonathan Taylor rushed 20 times for 95 yards and two touchdowns in the Colts’ Week 4 win over the Commanders.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

Playing in London, Taylor needed just 78 yards to overtake Travis Etienne as the league’s all-time leading rusher in international games. Taylor didn’t disappoint with his third multi-score effort of the season. Marcus Mariota left the game early and the Colts pulled away in the second half, allowing them to lean on the ground game. With the passing game struggling throughout the first month of football, expect the Colts to continue to build their offense around Taylor. He remains near the top of the RB1 ranks for his Week 5 matchup with the Steelers.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Raiders are “fully expecting” Brock Bowers (knee/illness) to play in Week 4 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Today’s report is in relation to Bowers’ illness, not his knee. Earlier this morning, the Raiders announced that Bowers has come down with an illness, but the illness will not alter his game status. Bowers’ knee was a non-issue last week, and we expect it to be a non-issue again this week. He is good to go for the Raiders’ Week 4 game against the Chiefs. Treat him like an elite TE1, as usual.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Eli Raridon (thigh) is active for Week 4 against the Bills.
item.description:
Eli Raridon NE Tight End

Raridon was questionable heading into the weekend, but he was able to get in three limited practice sessions this week, so he had been trending towards a return. He will back up Hunter Henry but could cut into Henry’s snaps enough to make Henry just a TE2 in deeper formats.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Patriots declared CB Christian Gonzalez, DT Christian Barmore, OT Dametrious Crownover, TE Tanner Arkin, QB Behren Morton, and CB Channing Canada inactive for Week 4 against the Bills.
item.description:
Dre'Mont Jones NE Linebacker

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel had announced Barmore and Gonzalez would miss this game a few days ago. However, this inactive list means that Dre’Mont Jones will return after missing the last two games. It’s a big boost for the Patriots defense, but we’re not usre it outweighs losing Gonzalez and Barmore.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Bills declared CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL T.J. Sanders, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 4 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Christian Benford BUF Cornerback

No real surprises here. Benford was listed as questionable heading into the day, but he didn’t practice at all this week so he was never likely to play. Rookie Davison Igbinosun is likely to step into his spot opposite Maxwell Hairston, which makes the Bills young and inexperienced on the boundary. Perhaps Drake Maye could finally take advantage of that on the way to his first truly good fantasy game of the season.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Giants declared RB Devin Singletary, S Ar’Darius Washington, CB Nikko Reed, DL Jihad Ward, OL J.C. Davis, TE Thomas Fidone, and DT Bobby Jamison-Travis as inactive for Week 4 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Devin Singletary NYG Running Back

This is the second-straight week that Singletary has been made a healthy scratch for the Giants. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy will serve as the backups to Cam Skattebo. It’s also worth noting that QB J.J. McCarthy, who was acquired from the Vikings earlier this week, is active for Week 4.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Texans declared LB Azeez Al-Shaair, DE Chris Braswell, OG Febechi Nwaiwu, OT Nate Thomas, and TE Marlin Klein inactive for Week 4 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Azeez Al-Shaair HOU Linebacker

The Texans are at near full strength and welcome back wide receiver Nico Collins, who was removed from the team’s injury report on Friday. Collins’ return comes at a time where Houston is seeking its first win of the season.

Source: Houston Texans

item.title: Bengals declared S Bryan Cook, S Kyle Dugger, LB Swayze Bozeman, OT Myles Hinton, WR Colbie Young, DT B.J. Hill, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 4 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Bryan Cook CIN Safety

Cook (ankle), Dugger (quad), Bozeman (groin), Young (knee), and Hill (Achilles) are all injury inactives for the Bengals. An improved defense will be without a pair of safeties and depth in the front seven will be tested against the Jaguars.

item.title: Bears declared QB Caleb Williams, OT Ozzy Trapilo, OG Jordan McFadden, DE Jamree Kromah, and DT Jayden Loving inactive for Week 4 against the Jets.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

Williams will miss another game, with Tyson Bagent likely to start for Chicago. D’Andre Swift, who missed some practice time this week, will suit up against a New York defense allowing the seventh lowest EPA per rush through three games.

Source: Kevin Fishbain

item.title: Bucs declared EDGE Rueben Bain, QB Baker Mayfield, CB Benjamin Morrison, TE Ko Kieft, DL DeMonte Capehart, G Billy Schrauth, and G Luke Haggard inactive for Week 4 against the Packers.
item.description:
Rueben Bain TB Outside Linebacker

Both Bain and Mayfield were ruled out earlier this week. UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels will make his starting debut against the Packers.

item.title: Cardinals LB Josh Sweat is active for Week 4 against the Giants.
item.description:
Josh Sweat ARI Outside Linebacker

Sweat entered this week listed as questionable but is officially active. The veteran pass rusher has yet to tally a sack in his first three games this season but should have plenty of opportunities to get after Jameis Winston this week. The Cardinals declared QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas V, S Rabbit Taylor-Demerson, OL Josh Fryar, and WR Reggie Virgil inactive for Week 4.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: Rams declared TE Colby Parkinson, WR CJ Daniels, QB Ty Simpson, CB Jaylen Watson, DT Aaron Donald, OL Bill Murray and CB Cam Lampkin inactive for Week 4 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson’s absence with knee and shoulder issues at least comes as Puka Nacua returns, though the Rams are somehow down to only two healthy tight ends. Parkinson appears to be genuinely day to day, so we would assume he has a decent chance of returning for Week 5 against the Bills. Improbably, the Rams’ injury issues have made Tyler Higbee a legitimate streaming option.

item.title: Packers declared OG Aaron Banks, OL Jacon Monk, DL Anthony Campbell, and RG Kevin Zeitler inactive for Week 4 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Aaron Banks GB Guard

Banks missed Week 1 with the knee issue. He suited up in Week 2 but aggravated the injury and has been out ever since. He is also dealing with a toe injury, per the injury report.

item.title: Cowboys declared LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Cobie Durant, CB Caelen Carson, RB Emari Demercado, OL James Houston, OL Ajani Cornelius, and WR Camden Brown inactive for Week 4 against the Texans.
item.description:
DeMarvion Overshown DAL Linebacker

Every player on here was ruled out before the weekend. The Cowboys continue have lost several key defenders through the early part of the season and will now have to find a way to slow a Houston offense that will have Nico Collins back for the first time in two weeks.

Source: Todd Archer

item.title: Jets declared WR Adonai Mitchell, RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LB Kiko Mauigoa, DE Kingsley Enagbare, OL Dylan Parham, and TE Mason Taylor inactive for Week 4 against the Bears.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

Mitchell will miss another game with his finger injury and Hall will be sidelined with a quad injury he sustained last week against the Lions. Garrett Wilson, with Mitchell out, should continue dominating air yards and targets in the balanced Jets offense. Braelon Allen will take over as New York’s lead back for now and should be in all fantasy lineups against a suspect Chicago run defense. Kenyon Sadiq has some streaming appeal with Mitchell out.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Jaguars declared CB Montaric Brown, WR CJ Williams, CB Christian Braswell, S Jalen Huskey, LB Jack Kiser, OL Daniel Faalele, and DE Wesley Williams inactive for Week 4 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Montaric Brown

Brown and Braswell entered the weekend questionable with hamstring and knee injuries, respectively. Both were limited practice participants this week but will not play against the Bengals.

item.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) is active for Week 4 against the Titans.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Flowers is officially active and can be treated as a fringe WR1 for fantasy purposes this week against the Titans. Flowers totaled five catches for 84 yards on six targets in limited action last week, and should see a few more routes than the 14 he ran last week. In addition to Flowers, the Ravens will also have left tackle Ronnie Stanley back after he missed last week’s game with a toe injury. The Ravens declared QB Joe Fagnano, WR Chris Moore, EDGE Trey Hendrickson, and DL Aeneas Peeblas inactive for Week 4.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Eagles RT Lane Johnson (personal) is out for Week 4 against the Rams.
item.description:
Lane Johnson PHI Tackle

The Eagles, of course, have a lengthy checkered history whenever Johnson is sidelined. 6-foot-9 rookie Markel Bell will take Johnson’s place vs. a Rams team that will be missing Aaron Donald in addition to an IRed Myles Garrett.

item.title: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is active for Week 4 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears is good to go for Sunday’s game against the Ravens after entering the weekend listed as questionable. He has totaled 99 scoreless yards from scrimmage this season on 17 touches, and has caught four passes on the year. Spears shouldn’t be considered as anything more than a fringe RB3/RB4 against a stout Ravens defense.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: Eagles declared WR DeVonta Smith, WR Hollywood Brown, TE Dallas Goedert, LB Zack Baun, QB Cole Payton S Marcus Epps, OT Lane Johnson and OT Fred Johnson inactive for Week 4 against the Rams.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

The question with Smith now becomes if he’s ready to return for Week 5 against the Jaguars. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo has reported it is unlikely. It’s a brutal, brutal development for fantasy managers who thought they were getting a breakout WR1 after Smith’s years of WR2 grinding. Dontayvion Wicks and first-round rookie Makai Lemon will try to pick up the targets slack, though veteran TE Zach Ertz will undoubtedly do some of the dirty work.

item.title: Jaylin Lane was carted off the field with a leg injury in Week 4 against the Colts.
item.description:
Jaylin Lane WAS Wide Receiver

Lane’s left knee was badly twisted under his body as he was being taken down on a kick return. He was carted off the field and several Commanders players came up the cart to console him. The team hasn’t made it official yet, but he will not return today.

item.title: Titans declared RB Michael Carter, CB Jaylon Jones, OG Drew Moss, OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, and DT Jackie Marshall inactive for Week 4 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Michael Carter TEN Running Back

Tyjae Spears was the only player of note carrying an injury designation into Week 4 for the Titans, and he is officially active. The 0-3 Titans hit the road to take on a stout Ravens defense that ranks 13th in yards allowed through the first three games of the season.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: Charles Omenihu suffered a groin injury in Week 4 against the Colts and will not return.
item.description:
Charles Omenihu WAS Defensive End

Omenihu signed a one-year deal with the Commanders as a rotational EDGE in the offseason. He had six pressures and five hurries heading into today’s game.

item.title: Marcus Mariota (knee) will not return in Week 4 against the Colts.
item.description:
Marcus Mariota WAS Quarterback

Per head coach Dan Quinn, Mariota re-injured the MCL in his right knee. He initially suffered the MCL injury during the preseason. The fact that he suffered a setback almost two months after the initial injury suggests this could be a long-term absence. It will be seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis for the rest of this game. The hope is that Jayden Daniels will be back for Week 5.

item.title: Lane Johnson (personal) is questionable for Week 4 against the Rams.
item.description:
Lane Johnson PHI Tackle

Johnson missing Week 4 would be a truly calamitous outcome for Philly. They are already without DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert, both of whom were ruled out on Saturday. Losing their starting right tackle would be another blow the struggling offense didn’t need. Rookie Markel Bell will be the next man up if Johnson is ruled out.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes Josh Sweat is “a player that will be of interest ot a lot of teams” ahead of the trade deadline.
item.description:
Josh Sweat ARI Outside Linebacker

Schefter named Khalil Mack as another pass-rusher who could be on the move for similar reasons. Both players are productive veteran EDGE defenders on teams struggling to win games right now. Mack will be a free agent next offseason, making him an easy trade target. Sweat is under contract through 2028 but made it clear this offseason that he was unhappy in Arizona.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes Tony Pollard “fits the profile” of a player who could be traded ahead of the deadline.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

Schefter didn’t cite any sources telling him that Pollard could be on the move, but he did connect a few key dots. Pollard is in the final year of his contract and the Titans are going nowhere fast. If they don’t plan on re-signing him next offseason, they might as well get something in return for him in the middle of another lost season. His departure would also clear the way for rookie Nick Singleton to see more work.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jerry Jeudy “could be had” before the trade deadline.
item.description:
Jerry Jeudy CLE Wide Receiver

With Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion earning large roles right away, Jeudy has all but vanished from the box scores. He went two games without catching a single pass before bringing down three balls for 36 yards on Thursday night. Jeudy got pushed out of the Browns’ long-term plans on draft night and isn’t even part of the week-to-week game plan at this point.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports teams are “doing their due diligence” on Marvin Harrison Jr.
item.description:
Marvin Harrison ARI Wide Receiver

Schefter noted that the Cardinals aren’t “enthralled” with the idea of trading Harrison Jr. He also said point-blank that “it would not be a surprise” for MHJ to be traded. As much as the Cardinals may not want to admit it, this experiment needs to come to an end. The team has Michael Wilson and Trey McBride locked up on long-term contracts and MHJ has done nothing this year. He has four catches for 73 scoreless yards this year. At this point, it’s likely in the best interest of both sides for Harrison Jr. to find a new home.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports “the hope is” that A.J. Brown (ankle) plays in Week 6.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Garfolo made it clear that this is what the team hopes will happen, but it’s far from a sure thing. Week 6 is the first week Brown is eligible to return from injured reserve. The Pats placed him on IR after he suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 1. Previous reports had Brown out for 6-8 weeks, so fantasy managers should be skeptical that he will be back for Week 6, but it’s at least on the table.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Tanne McKee is the Eagles’ backup quarterback for Week 4 against the Rams.
item.description:
Tanner McKee PHI Quarterback

The Eagles demoted Andy Dalton after his end zone interception in Week 3. He took over for Jalen Hurts while the latter was being evaluated for an injury and immediately gave the ball away in scoring position. McKee has two career starts since being drafted in 2023.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Marcus Mariota (knee) is questionable to return in Week 4 against the Colts.
item.description:
Marcus Mariota WAS Quarterback

Colts EDGE Laiatu Latu landed on Mariota’s right ankle while taking him down for a sack in the first quarter. Mariota was slow to get up and immediately made his way to the blue tent. He walked to the locker room after a brief stay in the tent. Seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis is under center for the Commanders.

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garfaolo reports DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is “at very best” questionable for Week 5 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Smith has already been ruled out for Week 4. The Eagles take on the Jags in London next week. It sounds like fantasy managers should be prepared to be without their start receiver for that contest as well. Dontayvion Wicks currently profiles as the team’s top wideout, but it’s hard to imagine the team not getting first-round rookie Makai Lemon more involved as well. Both players are solid FLEX options for Week 4.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jadeveon Clowney (knee) is expected to play in Week 4 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Jadeveon Clowney HOU Defensive End

Clowney hasn’t played since injuring his knee in Week 1. Though he isn’t expected to be a major factor in the Texans’ plans, Houston’s defense hasn’t been the shutdown unit that it was last year. They currently rank as a below-average team in EPA per play allowed. Clowney won’t change their fortunes overnight, but he will hopefully help them make incremental improvements.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tyjae Spears (ankle) is expected to play in Week 4 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears played through the ankle issue last week and there was no indication during this week’s practice that he suffered any sort of setback. He is good to go for Week 4, though fantasy managers can’t count on him for much. He touched the ball just three times last week.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Bears placed Braxton Jones (knee) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Braxton Jones CHI Offensive Lineman

Jones injured his knee and was considered “week to week” going forward. The good news is that this means it won’t be season-ending IR, but the Bears will be without their starting left tackle for at least four games. Theo Benedet will start in his place this week. Now healthy, Ozzy Trapilo could take over that job in the coming weeks as well.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Monroe Freeling (concussion) will play in Week 4 against the Lions.
item.description:
Monroe Freeling CAR OFFENSIVE TACKLE (SUB)

The Panthers entered the season down both of their starting tackles. They will also be without left guard Damien Lewis this week. Getting Freeling back is a big win for Bryce Young and the offense. Freeling has struggled in pass protection so far but is serviceable in the run game.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Dre Greenlaw (quad) is expected to play in Week 4 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Dre Greenlaw SF Linebacker

The 49ers are already banged up on defense with Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams ruled out on Friday. Greenlaw was listed as questionable after getting in a single limited practice. He has 22 combined tackles, 11 defensive stops, and one pressure this year.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Derrick Harmon (foot) “is expected to miss a few weeks.”
item.description:
Derrick Harmon PIT Defensive Tackle

Rapoport noted that IR is an option, but the injury is not considered long-term. Harmon suffered the foot injury on Thursday against the Browns. He was carted to the locker room and was later spotted wearing a boot on the sidelines. The second-year tackle had 1.5 sacks in three games before leaving Week 4 early. His potential breakout campaign will now be put on hold for upwards of a month.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sam LaPorta and the Lions “have broken off contract talks.”
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

Rapoport did note that the Lions could make another push to sign LaPorta later this year, so the door isn’t entirely closed. LaPorta is set to become a free agent next offseason. The team could, however, place the franchise tag on him. He has gotten off to a quiet start with 14 catches for 144 yards and one score. LaPorta is currently on pace for a career-low in yards per game. He would still have plenty of suitors in free agency, even if the counting stats don’t improve this year.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Baker Mayfield (thumb) is expected to miss “anywhere from three to six weeks.”
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Previous reports put the timeline at 2-4 weeks, so it’s possible the injury is worse than initially expected. The good news is that testing revealed no ligament or tendon damage in Mayfield’s thumb. Per Schefter, Mayfield’s return will depend on how quickly he can grip the ball. That is typically the first step in throwing a football. For now, UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels will draw the start. He is worth a look in Superflex leagues but can’t be played in one-quarterback formats.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ladd McConkey (foot) is likely to play in Week 4 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey was limited in Wednesday’s practice, downgraded to a DNP on Thursday, and returned for another limited session on Friday. It looks like the team was just heavily managing his workload during the week, but that could continue into today’s game. McConkey has been the only modestly successful part of the offense this year, and the Chargers would be wise to keep him healthy, even if that means limiting his snaps. He remains in the WR2 mix, though the injury makes him a riskier bet than usual.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Rams “do not intend to limit” Puka Nacua’s workload in Week 4 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Looks like we’ve got ourselves an old-fashioned source-off here. Schefter says Nacua won’t be limited, while The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero said over the weekend that Nacua may be on “a stricter snap count than usual.” Even if his snaps are cut back, Nacua is one of the best per-route receivers in the NFL. He will get by for fantasy managers in whatever role the Rams give him. He is, at worst, a low-end WR1 for Week 4.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jalen Coker (quad) is “unlikely to play” in Week 4 against the Lions.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker injured his quad in Week 3. He got in two limited practices this week before being listed as questionable. It doesn’t sound like a long-term injury, but the team is being cautious with a young wideout who has already suffered multiple lower-body injuries this year. With Xavier Legette on IR, Brycen Tremayne is Carolina’s WR2 for Week 4.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Zay Flowers (hamstring) is “good to go” for Week 4 against the Titans.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Fowler added that Flowers is not expected to be on a “hard pitch count.” The Ravens will presumably keep tabs on his injured hamstring, but as long as he feels good, Flowers will get his normal allotment of snaps. Despite exiting Week 1 early and being on a snap count last week, Flowers is averaging six catches for 117 yards across two appearances this year. He will make the WR1 cut next week if he puts up similar numbers today.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Ashton Dulin (ankle) will play in Week 4 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Ashton Dulin IND Wide Receiver

With Keenan Allen ruled out and Alec Pierce on IR, Dulin is now in line to be the Colts’ No. 2 receiver in his season debut. The passing attack will run through Josh Downs, putting him comfortably inside the WR2 ranks. Inactive for the Colts are WR Keenan Allen, WR Darius Slayton, RB DJ Giddens, QB Riley Leonard, EDGE George Gumbs, and OG Dalton Tucker.

item.title: Commanders declared Terry McLaurin (hamstring) inactive for Week 4 against the Colts.
item.description:
Terry McLaurin WAS Wide Receiver

McLaurin was a late addition to the injury report after tweaking his hamstring on Friday. He was initially expected to play through the issue, but things took a turn for the worse over the weekend. Stefon Diggs will operate as the team’s clear No. 1 receiver until McLaurin is back. Inactive for the Commanders are QB Jayden Daniels, RB Rachaad White, WR Luke McCaffrey, S Nick Cross, EDGE Javontae Jean-Baptiste, and OG Sam Cosmi.

item.title: Panthers elevated WR Ja’Seem Reed from the practice squad.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

This is notable considering head coach Dave Canales previously said that the team would only elevated Reed if Coker couldn’t go in Week 4. Coker, listed as questionable, now appears on the worse side of the designation ahead of a Week 4 meeting with the Lions on Sunday Night Football. Fantasy managers are better off making contingent plans now considering the Panthers are the penultimate game of the week.

item.title: Panthers placed WR Xavier Legette (knee) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Xavier Legette CAR Wide Receiver

Legette was already ruled out for Week 4, which marks his second straight absence. He will now be forced to miss the next four games while on injured reserve, making his absence a total of five games, at minimum. John Metchie and Brycen Tremaine will continue to operate as the WR3 in the interim.

item.title: Seahawks placed RB Jadarian Price (chest) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

Price reportedly aggravated a chest injury during the team’s Wednesday practice and will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he tends to the injury. The backfield will be left in the hands of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani in Week 4 against the Chargers but should get reinforcements in short order with Zach Charbonnet set to resume practicing. Price’s season continues to trend poorly for fantasy managers that invested a mid-round pick in his services this summer.

item.title: Saints TE Noah Fant (abdominal) is questionable for Week 4 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Noah Fant NO Tight End

So too is LB Pete Werner, while LB Kaden Elliss, DE Carl Granderson, and DEAnfernee Jennings have been ruled out. Rookie tight end Oscar Delp would be in line to see additional run alongside Juwan Johnson, should Fant be unable to play.

item.title: Falcons DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and LB Divine Deablo (hamstring) are questionable for Week 4 against the Saints.
item.description:
Samson Ebukam ATL Defensive End

Ebukam and Deablo are the only two players listed on the Falcons’ injury report for their Week 4 divisional showdown agains the Saints on Monday Night Football. Ebukam returned to a full practice Saturday for the first time since injuring his hamstring in practice ahead of Week 3. The Falcons remain relatively healthy as they prepare to challenge the Saints for the division lead through the first month of play.

item.title: Bears QB Tyson Bagent will start in Week 4 against the Jets, reports Dan Wiederer of the Athletic.
item.description:
Tyson Bagent CHI Quarterback

Bagent came in after Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring strain in Week 2, but missed Week 3 as he was in concussion protocol with Case Keenum getting the start. With Williams still out, Bagent will be back under center against the Jets. With Ben Johnson calling plays, Bagent is a super-flex option in Week 4.

Source: Dan Wiederer

item.title: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is likely to miss Week 4 against the Colts, reports Commanders beat writer Ben Standig.
item.description:
Terry McLaurin WAS Wide Receiver

McLaurin injured his hamstring at practice on Friday. While there was initially optimism he could play through the injury, McLaurin is now likely to miss the game against the Colts, according to Standig. Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams should serve as the Commanders’ top wide receivers with Marcus Mariota under center in Week 4.

Source: Ben Ständig

item.title: Colts WR Keenan Allen (groin) is out for Week 4 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Keenan Allen IND Wide Receiver

Allen was limited in practice throughout the week and listed as questionable. Now he’s been ruled out for Week 4 against the Commanders. Josh Downs is locked in as the Colts top wide receiver this week and Tyler Warren should also see a boost in value with Allen sidelined.

item.title: Lions S Brian Branch (Achilles) has a “really good chance” to return to practice next week, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
item.description:
Brian Branch DET Defensive Back

Branch is still on the PUP list after tearing his Achilles last season. Lions HC Dan Campbell said Branch was close to returning to practice on Friday, though he wouldn’t disclose when exactly the Lions will open the 21-day practice window for the 24-year-old safety. According to Pelissero, there’s a really good chance Branch returns to practice next week. He’ll undoubtedly help a Lions pass defense that has been torn to shreds in the first three weeks of the season.

item.title: Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield (thumb) could return against the Steelers in Week 6, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield dislocated his thumb in Week 3’s loss against the Vikings. The 31-year-old quarterback had no ligament or tendon damage. According to Pelissero, it would be tough but not impossible for Mayfield to return in Week 5, making Week 6 against the Steelers the more likely return date. Jalon Daniels will start for the Buccaneers against the Packers in Week 4.

item.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) may be on “stricter snap count than usual” in Week 4 against the Eagles, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Rams HC Sean McVay said Nacua, who has been dealing with a groin injury, is good to go after getting a full practice in on Friday. The coach also noted that they’re still working through Nacua’s snap count and now Pelissero reports that it could be stricter than usual. Fantasy managers should still treat Nacua as a high-end WR1 even in a difficult matchup against the Eagles in Week 4.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) isn’t expected to practice next week and could return in November, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

Parsons is coming back from tearing his ACL late last season. The 27-year-old defensive end didn’t practice this week and isn’t expected to practice next week, according to Pelissero. Parsons hasn’t had any setbacks in his rehab, but still isn’t ready for the Packers to open the 21-day window for him to practice before he’s activated. Pelissero points out that it could be November before Parsons is ready for game action. Green Bay is 1-2 this year and 1-8 without Parsons in the lineup over the last two years (including playoffs).

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Vikings WR Justin Jefferson (ankle) is “hopeful” to return in Week 5 against the Saints, reports ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

Jefferson suffered an ankle injury in Week 3’s win over the Buccaneers. He didn’t practice this week and has already been ruled out for Week 4 against the Dolphins. According to Fowler, the Vikings are “hopeful” Jefferson could return next week against the Saints and don’t believe the injury will be a long-term issue. In the meantime, Jordan Addison will serve as the WR1 this week against Miami.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels (elbow) could play in Week 5 against the Giants, reports Jonathan Jones of the Athletic.
item.description:
Jayden Daniels WAS Quarterback

Daniels practiced in a limited capacity this week, but will ultimately sit out the Week 4 matchup against the Colts. According to Jones, sources in Washington believe Daniels could return in Week 5 against the Giants if he gets in a full week of practice this week. While Daniels is going to play through the same elbow injury he had last year, offseason surgery hasn’t been ruled out. Marcus Mariota will continue to start under center for the Commanders in Daniels’ absence.

Source: Jonathan Jones

item.title: Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla said he has “no current plans to change anything about the team, including the coach, president, operation or Lumen Field.”
item.description:
Vinod Khosla SEA Owner

Axios’ Dan Primack reminded Khosla of his stated desire to preserve what Paul Allen built before asking him if he would commit to keeping the Seahawks in Seattle long term. Khosla first responded by saying he would “never say never,” and then rhetorically wondered aloud whether this team would be in Seattle “500 years from now,” before making his “no current plans” remarks. Primack helpfully refocused the conversation on the Lumen Field lease’s 2032 end date, prompting Khosla to say that he doesn’t think he’ll “do anything but learn for a while.” Seriously entertaining a move seems unlikely, but Khosla would do well to provide a more concrete answer to a city that once saw its NBA team relocated after new ownership took over. His comments can be ignored for now. Perhaps this is just an early negotiation tactic for future stadium renovations.

Source: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk

item.title: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams need more from Blake Corum in the coming weeks.
item.description:
Blake Corum

Atkins believes Puka Nacua’s (groin) impending return will lighten the box, in turn making life easier on the run game and preventing the opposition from blitzing as frequently as the Broncos did last week. Corum has not established himself as a reliable weekly contributor in fantasy. Perhaps positive impacts from Nacua’s return trickle down to the Rams’ No. 2 running back. Kyren Williams remains a locked-in starter. Keep Corum stashed for now.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Aaron Donald is dealing with a “mild” back injury.
item.description:
Aaron Donald

Rapoport also said Donald’s absence is more than just a precautionary measure, and compared his sidelining to the way the Rams handled Myles Garrett’s knee injury, with a long-term view in mind. Check back next week to see if Donald is feeling well enough to resume practicing.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that QB Tyson Bagent is expected to start for the Bears in Week 4 against the Jets.
item.description:
Tyson Bagent CHI Quarterback

Bagent signed a two-year, $10 million contract extension in August 2025 to serve as the Bears’ No. 2 quarterback. He took the majority of first-team reps this week despite QB3 Case Keenum’s Week 3 heroics. Bagent can be started in Superflex leagues against the Jets, assuming he is officially named the starter this weekend.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Derwin James (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 4 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Derwin James LAC Safety

James sandwiched a Thursday absence with two limited sessions. The veteran safety plays through injuries whenever possible, and the Chargers will need all hands on deck to get their season back on track.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said the team is making sure Zach Charbonnet (knee) “feels great when the time comes for him to come back.”
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

The Seahawks opened Charbonnet’s practice window on Thursday, but he is not yet ready to return. Charbonnet’s left quad is noticeably thinner than his right quad, and Macdonald explained that there is “a process to get him physically and mentally ready to go.” That said, Macdonald also said the veteran running back “looks fantastic.” Stash him now.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Chiefs ruled out LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 4 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Josh Simmons KC Tackle

Earlier this week, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Simmons is dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back. Brutal. On the plus side, CB Chamarri Conner (knee) will make his return.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Marvin Mims (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Marvin Mims DEN Wide Receiver

Mims aggravated his foot injury back in Week 1 and has been inactive on game day since. The Broncos’ volatile performer is back, but is not on the FLEX radar in 12-team formats.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: J.K. Dobbins (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the 49ers.
item.description:
J.K. Dobbins DEN Running Back

Dobbins practiced in full this week, so he should be ready to handle his typical workload against the 49ers this week. The Broncos’ lead rusher has played very unproductively this season, failing to hit 7.0 PPR points each week. The Broncos’ defensive line has been hit hard by injuries. Perhaps Dobbins can steady himself in the RB2/FLEX ranks against them.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (foot) is not on the injury report for Week 4 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle gave folks a fright, sporting a walking boot after the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams. He practiced in full all week, though, so there are no concerns about his availability. Waddle is a WR2 against the 49ers in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: Joey Porter (back/conditioning/contract) is not on the injury report for Week 4 against the Texans.
item.description:
Joey Porter DAL Cornerback

Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said on Friday, “we actually think Joey Porter will get snaps.” ESPN’s Todd Archer notes that prior to the mid-week trade, Porter was ruled out of Thursday’s game between the Steelers and Browns, saying his back was tight. He practiced the last two days “without issue.” Porter might be on a snap count this week, but it looks like he will play.

Source: Todd Archer

item.title: Free agent RB Terrell Jennings worked out for the Steelers on Friday.
item.description:
Terrell Jennings PIT Running Back

Perhaps one of the Steelers’ backup running backs got dinged up in their Thursday Night Football game against the Browns. Adding Jennings would make sense for depth.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: 49ers LT Trent Williams (stinger) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Trent Williams SF Tackle

The 49ers will have their stud left tackle active on Sunday. 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw (quad bruise) is questionable to play. 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) and DL Mykel Williams (knee) have both been ruled out.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans (ribs) will be a game-time decision for Week 4 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans is officially questionable to play. He did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but in uniform and did some running on the side in the early, open portion of Friday’s practice. The grizzled veteran tends to play through injuries. He will try to play this week while wearing a compression shirt with padding in it. Evans told reporters that he has played through a similar injury previously. If active, he carries obvious re-injury risk but warrants starting as a WR2.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Rams placed Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

This escalated quickly. Ferguson briefly returned in Week 3 after getting X-rays on his injured ankle, but he was ultimately unable to continue. Ferguson can be kept on squads possessing an injured reserve spot, but dropping him for a needed starter makes sense. He will be eligible to return in Week 8 against the Chargers.

Source: Los Angeles Rams

item.title: Cardinals EDGE Josh Sweat (groin) is questionable to play in Week 4 against the Giants.
item.description:
Josh Sweat ARI Outside Linebacker

Sweat practiced fully on Thursday before downgrading to limited on Friday, indicating he may have strained his groin during the Cardinals’ final Week 4 practice. He still has a chance to play. His potential absence would benefit the Giants’ passing attack.

Source: Bo Brack

item.title: Chargers DL Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Dalvin Tomlinson LAC Defensive Lineman

This was supposed to be a Jadarian Price FLEX redemption game, but with him on the ropes, it instead looks like it will be George Holani and Emanuel Wilson as reasonable FLEX plays for Week 4.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Eagles.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

He didn’t practice at any point this week with an AC sprain suffered after he had already been questionable with the knee ailment heading into Week 3. Tyler Higbee should be a reasonable TE2 option against the Eagles this week even if Parkinson is healthy; it doesn’t seem like he is.

item.title: Brenen Thompson (quad) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Brenen Thompson LAC Wide Receiver

Thompson didn’t play last week with the quad issue and may be an IR candidate over the weekend. He hasn’t practiced in either of the last two weeks. He has one catch for 13 yards in 22 offensive snaps so far. You may cut bait in non-dynasty leagues.

item.title: Seahawks S Julian Love (calf) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Julian Love SEA Safety

Love returns after a one-game absence. Fellow starting S Ty Okada (hamstring) is questionable to play, though he is seemingly on the wrong side of questionable. Okada has not yet played in 2026 and may need to log consecutive full practice sessions before suiting up on game day.

Source: Gregg Bell

item.title: Keaton Mitchell (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

He practiced all three days this week, upgrading to full on Friday, and should be a lower-end FLEX option against a tough Seahawks run defense. The good news for Mitchell is that the proof-of-concept of “the Chargers can’t run block so they should just use someone fast” worked in Week 3. He should see a reasonable amount of touches in Week 4.

item.title: Ladd McConkey (foot) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey was limited in Wednesday’s practice, didn’t practice on Thursday, and was listed as an observer despite a generous “limited” tag on Friday. Either way, not a great trend. McConkey should be treated as a true question mark. If he’s ruled out, Tre’ Harris and Quentin Johnston would get a boost, but given how the Chargers have played it’s hard to start anyone into the Seattle defense.

item.title: Seahawks rule out Jadarian Price (chest) for Week 4 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

Price reportedly aggravated his chest injury on Wednesday. That is unfortunate. With Price out of the picture against the Chargers, and Zach Charbonnet (knee) still rehabbing, burly RB Emanuel Wilson and receiving specialist RB George Holani will split backfield reps. Wilson can be started as a volume-based RB2/FLEX while Holani is FLEX-viable in PPR formats.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Bengals ruled out WR Colbie Young (knee) for Week 4 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Colbie Young CIN Wide Receiver

With WR Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve, WR Dohnte Meyers should operate as the Bengals’ No. 3 wide receiver this week. He is not reliable enough to warrant FLEX consideration in 12-team leagues, though.

Source: Cincinnati Bengals

item.title: Bengals RG Dalton Risner (knee) is questionable to play in Week 4 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Dalton Risner CIN Guard

Risner is one of the Bengals’ best offensive linemen, profiling as an all-around talented run blocker and pass protector. He sat out on Wednesday and Thursday before practicing in full on Friday. He seemingly has a chance to play. Having him on the field would be very helpful against the Jaguars.

Source: Cincinnati Bengals

item.title: Andrew Thomas (groin) is not on New York’s final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

Thomas is on the Terron Armstead plan — very limited practice reps, zero chance of him missing the game. He only got in a limited session on Friday after a pair of DNPs on Wednesday and Thursday. It does not actually seem to matter. Thomas will go.

item.title: Tyrone Tracy (knee) is not on New York’s final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
Tyrone Tracy NYG Running Back

Tracy upgraded to a full practice session, but looks to have lost most of his backup work to Najee Harris at this point. Tracy does not need to be kept in shallow leagues, but at least he’s good to play.

item.title: Lamar Jackson (back) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

As noted yesterday, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes Jackson’s reps in practice going forward will be managed at his behest, so don’t get too startled on Wednesday if he’s limited again. Jackson is an obvious overall QB1 candidate in Week 4 against the Titans.

item.title: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 4 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears played through the injury last week. This week, he went DNP, LP and FP, so he is seemingly on track to play. Regardless, he is a low-floor, touchdown-dependent FLEX against the Ravens this week.

Source: Tennessee Titans

item.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 4 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

They added an “NIR/rest” to Flowers’ listing on the injury report on Friday and he had a limited session after going full on Thursday. We’re not going to believe this is serious news without one of the league’s sourced men or women saying it is. Flowers profiles as a WR1 against the lowly Titans.

item.title: Tony Pollard (ankle) is not on the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

With Titans RB2 Tyjae Spears (ankle) questionable to play, Pollard could end up handling a big workload. Unfortunately, the Titans field an unproductive offense and face the Ravens this week. He can only be viewed as a moderate FLEX starter.

Source: Tennessee Titans

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

He should be trusted as a low-end WR3/FLEX play against the Bengals. Meyers has cleared the injury report with this thumb listing three times in three weeks, though he was questionable in Week 2. It clearly isn’t bothering him enough to impact his play.

item.title: Texans G Ed Ingram (groin) is questionable for Houston’s Week 4 game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Ed Ingram HOU Guard

He got in a full session today and was limited on Wednesday and Thursday. Ingram is the team’s best run blocker, so it would behoove them greatly for him to be active after two weeks where David Montgomery and Woody Marks were dead on arrival in the backfield.

item.title: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

Wright sits atop the Dolphins’ depth chart with De’Von Achane (knee) done for the year. He will likely split touches with new No. 2 running back Ollie Gordon in a very difficult matchup against the Vikings this week. Both players are worth rostering, but they are shaky FLEX starters this week.

Source: Barry Jackson

item.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) is not on Houston’s final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

He got in a full session and will escape the line. Collins doesn’t play the same amount of snaps that most of the league’s top wideouts play anyway, so even if he is managed a bit, he can be trusted as a low-end WR1 in what looks to be a smash spot against a bad Cowboys pass defense, though one that is integrating new trade acquisition Joey Porter Jr. against Collins.

item.title: Zack Baun (concussion) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 4 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Zack Baun PHI Linebacker

Not ideal timing as they gear up to try to stop Kyren Williams and Blake Corum on the ground. Baun did not practice all week and his availability for Week 5 is in some question as things stand. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. will likely get extra reps next to Jihaad Campbell, though Campbell is also questionable with a knee injury.

item.title: Chris Bell (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

Bell posted a 4/67 receiving line last week, though the Dolphins are still managing his reps. The Vikings’ blitz-based defense poses problems for Miami, limiting Bell to WR4 status this week. The rookie wide receiver should be rostered in 12-team formats.

Source: Barry Jackson

item.title: Will Shipley (foot) is not on Philadelphia’s final injury report for Week 4.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

It’s a surprising twist after Shipley missed both of the first two practices of the week; he got in a full session today and seems likely to be more involved as a pass-catcher with DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert down. Even with that, he’ll struggle to find FLEX value against the Rams.

item.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 4 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

He didn’t practice all week and will again be replaced by the combination of Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt in Week 4. Neither of those players are particularly appealing options, though Ertz has enough of a history of success and the Eagles are bereft enough of targets to make him a viable TE2.

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 4 game against the Rams.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Smith didn’t practice at all this week and enters Week 5 in a precarious position. Dontayvion Wicks should take over as the team’s No. 1 receiver, and it’s possible Makai Lemon will get more involved as well as the Eagles try to stay above .500 against the Rams.

item.title: Brock Bowers (knee) is not on the injury report for Week 4 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers was not on the injury report Wednesday and Thursday. The Raiders limited him on Friday. Last week, he logged two limited sessions before sitting out on Friday. The improvement is encouraging, but it is worth mentioning that the team is still managing his reps during each week’s final practice. He should be treated as an elite TE1, as usual.

Source: Paul H. Gutierrez

item.title: Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) is not on New York’s final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
Minkah Fitzpatrick NYJ Safety

The veteran safety should be good to go for the Jets against the Bears in Week 4. Fitzpatrick wound up missing two weeks with a mild groin injury.

item.title: Kenyon Sadiq (back) is questionable for New York’s Week 4 game against the Bears.
item.description:
Kenyon Sadiq NYJ Tight End

He did get in another limited session today, his third in a row, which would suggest he has a strong chance of playing. Sadiq will get a rankings boost with Breece Hall, Adonai Mitchell, and Mason Taylor all ruled out. He’s a fringe TE1, but one with an extremely high ceiling after last week’s 7/105/1 line.

item.title: Rueben Bain Jr. (shoulder/groin) will not play in Tampa Bay’s Week 4 game against Green Bay.
item.description:
Rueben Bain TB Outside Linebacker

The old NFC Central rivalry will not be renewed by rookie EDGE player Bain, who has now missed two weeks in a row and does not yet look close to returning.

item.title: Bucky Irving (glute) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
Bucky Irving TB Running Back

He finally got in a full session on Friday after a pair of limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Irving will be hard to trust with Jalon Daniels under center in Week 4 but the volume should still be there to get him on the low-end RB2 line.

item.title: Chris Godwin (ankle) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
Chris Godwin TB Wide Receiver

Godwin was a full participant for two straight days after a Wednesday DNP. The insertion of Jalon Daniels makes him (well, makes every Buccaneers player) hard to trust for Week 4, but Godwin is probably still in the FLEX conversation.

item.title: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports that Ladd McConkey (foot) is present at practice but did not participate in the portion of practice open to the media on Friday.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

Rhim shared a photo showing McConkey fully suited up in pads and a helmet, ostensibly ready for practice, but he didn’t run any routes or catch any passes with the rest of the Chargers’ wide receivers early on. We expect to see McConkey listed as a limited participant later today, but he seems to be truly questionable to play at this time. Stay tuned.

Source: Kris Rhim

item.title: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Charlie Kolar LAC Tight End

He did rejoin practice today, making it plausible he’ll be up for the Chargers’ Week 5 game against the Broncos. Second-year receiving TE Oronde Gadsden was unable to seize the moment with Kolar and TE David Njoku (knee) sidelined last week, catching 0-of-3 targets. The once-promising youngster must do something on Sunday if he wishes to remain re-draft-relevant in 12-team formats.

Source: Kris Rhim

item.title: Bears ruled out CB Kyler Gordon (calf) for Week 4 against the Jets.
item.description:
Kyler Gordon CHI Defensive Back

Gordon, LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and EDGE Shemar Stewart (knee) are all in the process of returning from the reserve/physically unable to perform list. None of them will play this week. Fill-in starting DB Cam Lewis (hip) is doubtful.

item.title: Bears ruled out LT Braxton Jones (knee) for Week 4 against the Jets.
item.description:
Braxton Jones CHI Offensive Lineman

Jones is unable to play, and OT Ozzy Trapilo (knee) is not yet ready to return from his 2025 season-ending injury, so OT Theo Benedet gets the start on the left side. As far as backups go, Benedet is solid. He generally fares better as a run blocker than as a pass protector, though.

Source: Jason Lieser

item.title: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) is questionable for New England’s Week 4 game against the Bills.
item.description:
Eli Raridon NE Tight End

He got in three limited sessions this week. If active, Raridon would cut into Hunter Henry’s ceiling a bit.

item.title: D’Andre Swift (knee) is not on the injury report for Week 4 against the Jets.
item.description:
D'Andre Swift CHI Running Back

Swift sat out on Thursday with a knee issue, but he resumed practicing on Friday. Fantasy managers should expect him to handle his normal, featured role. The Bears’ starting running back has totaled at least 19 carries and targets combined in each game this season. He is a bankable, high-end RB2.

Source: Kevin Fishbain

item.title: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said it’s too early to say whether WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. (undisclosed) will resume practicing next week.
item.description:
Dont'e Thornton LV Wide Receiver

The lanky speedster was placed on injured reserve late in August. He is not exceptionally talented, but he can contribute meaningfully to an NFL offense. Getting him back would help keep safeties honest. Stay tuned.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Raiders ruled out RG Jackson Powers-Johnson (groin) for Week 4 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Jackson Powers-Johnson LV Offensive Lineman

The Raiders will be without their star right guard for this divisional showdown. It’s an unfortunate loss. The Chiefs’ defensive tackle group is talented. Hopefully, Powers-Johnson can return in time for the Raiders’ Week 5 game against the Patriots.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Rams ruled out Aaron Donald (back) for Week 4 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Aaron Donald

Donald was unable to practice on Wednesday and Thursday. His participation level on Friday has not yet been released, but clearly, he isn’t feeling up to playing this week. The Rams will also be without their No. 2 perimeter CB Jaylen Watson (shoulder).

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle) for Week 4 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson suffered the ankle injury in Week 3 against the Broncos and was taken to the locker room for X-rays. He was cleared to return, but only did so briefly. The intriguing youngster remains a worthwhile hold, but he could end up being questionable to play next week.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (groin) is “good to go” for Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Eagles.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua will return after getting in a Friday full practice and should be a WR1 play, even against the Eagles’ vaunted secondary. McVay noted that they are still working through how they will navigate his snap count, so Davante Adams should remain near the WR1 line this week as they reintegrate Nacua. But nobody is sitting Puka Nacua in a standard league.

Source: Stu Jackson

item.title: Justin Jefferson (ankle) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 4 game against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

He didn’t practice at any point this week despite optimistic words from Kevin O’Connell and company. O’Connell said he just “couldn’t get there” this week and he will receive treatment over the weekend. The Vikings coach also noted next week — Jefferson’s return to New Orleans after a storied college career at LSU — is a “big one for him next week.” If they were going to rest him against one team, the lowly Dolphins make sense. Jordan Addison will get a bump and Jauan Jennings could be a FLEX option against Miami.

item.title: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) is questionable for Week 4 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Keenan Allen IND Wide Receiver

This one went under the radar. Allen was limited on Wednesday with a “rest” designation. He remained limited on Thursday, but the Colts tacked a groin injury next to his name while maintaining the “rest” designation and hope for a Week 4 appearance along the way. Allen was downgraded on Friday, unable to practice, and should be considered truly questionable to face the Commanders this week. Were he to sit, No. 1 wide receiver Josh Downs would get a helpful target share boost.

Source: Indianapolis Colts

item.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said it’s still not “the right time” for James Conner (ankle) to return.
item.description:
James Conner ARI Running Back

Same goes for TE Tip Reiman (ankle). LaFleur said he does not check in with the medical staff about them “on the daily,” but he “knows they’re doing well.” Neither player needs to be rostered in 12-team formats. Conner may be fantasy-relevant later in the year, but a lot would have to go wrong beforehand for that to be the case.

Source: PHNX Cardinals

item.title: 49ers principal owner Jed York has been suspended for six games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy.
item.description:
Jed York SF Center

York offered the following statement: “To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry. This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility.” This wouldn’t appear to have any on-field impact for the 49ers. York will be able to attend games again starting in Week 10.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is not on Buffalo’s final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

He’ll be good to go against the Christian Gonzalez-less Patriots. Moore is evidently still dealing with some soreness as he practiced in a non-contact jersey at points this week, but he’ll be a worthy WR2 in an elevated matchup.

item.title: Keaton Mitchell (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 4 injury report.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

He practiced all three days this week and should be a lower-end FLEX option against a tough Seahawks run defense. The good news for Mitchell is that the proof-of-concept of “the Chargers can’t run block so they should just use someone fast” worked in Week 3. He should see a reasonable amount of touches in Week 4.

item.title: Bills coach Joe Brady said WR Keon Coleman (ankle) “should be good to play” for Buffalo’s Week 4 game against the Patriots.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Coleman was limited on Thursday after a Wednesday DNP and apparently will avoid a questionable tag. He was questionable last week and played through the injury, though he doesn’t draw enough targets to be fantasy-relevant outside of the deepest leagues at this point.

Source: Jay Skurski

item.title: Bills coach Joe Brady said CB Christian Benford (toe) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 4 game against the Patriots.
item.description:
Christian Benford BUF Cornerback

Despite the questionable listing, Benford did not appear in the media portion of practice on Friday. At best, he’ll be listed as limited later today. Benford seems to be on the pessimistic side of questionable for Week 4.

Source: Jay Skurski

item.title: Ravens DL Trey Hendrickson (finger) underwent surgery and will not play in Baltimore’s Week 4 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Trey Hendrickson BAL Outside Linebacker
